steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat together sugar, butter, and eggs in a large bowl with an electric mixer on low speed.
Blend in flour. Mix in milk, 1/2 cup at a time. Add 1 cup coconut flakes and vanilla; mix well.
Pour filling into unbaked pie crust. Sprinkle top with 1 tablespoon coconut flakes.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is set and coconut is toasted, 40 to 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Custard Pie
raw_recipe.description: This coconut custard pie has a rich, creamy custard filling in a flaky pie crust topped with toasted coconut for a wonderful old-fashioned dessert.

review.reviewBody:
After altering the recipe a little, (half & half instead of milk & 3/4 cup sugar) this recipe was great tasting and easy to make!

I made it for my mom's 50th Birthday, her favorite kind of pie that she hadn't had in over 30 years... what a challenge this would be, I thought ( I cook... but am not much of a baker...to say the least). What a fabulous outcome! Even made my dad proud !!!!(pie making is a dying art in my family that he has completely mastered... the women who cook and alter recipes tend not to do so well in this department, but this was a real winner!).

This was a request, I'm not a fan of coconut, but I'm told it is PERFECTION!

I read the reviews and reduced the Sugar to 1c and changed the milk to half & half. I also took the advice of others and mixed the ingredients as intended. Then I added tin foil to the crust after 15 minutes.

As far as setting? It comes out toothpick clean after 50 minutes but still shifts in the pan, so I let it really set in the fridge overnight. The recipe should really suggest this. It was perfect after that and should be chilled.

I just finished mixing another (SO simple & easy) and am licking the bowl myself. It's delicious.

Some claimed greasy? I didn't reduce the butter, but I did soften it (leave out or microwave for 10 seconds). I think the greasy taste may be from lumps that settled, then melted when baking. Soften and blend til smooth. This worked for me, not greasy AT ALL, just YUMMY!

I'm going to try this custard recipe and use blueberries or raspberries instead of the coconut. I think that will be delicious.

I liked this pie after making some alterations. It is not really a coconut custard pie...it is a coconut pie, with 2 eggs, it is just held together with the help of a ton of butter. Since I was using sweetened coconut, I decreased the sugar to 3/4 cup. I used half & half instead of milk, I forgot the flour; but there may have been enough left over on the pie shell. The most important thing: I decreased cooking heat to 300, covered the whole pie with foil and checked it every 30 minutes. In all, I think it took 75 minutes to cook, the last 15, I uncovered it and put it up to 350. It is good, very sweet; but I still think I prefer a more custardy pie with more eggs.

After reading the reviews, I did cut down on the sugar. I used 1 cup. When I make again, I will probably cut it down to 3/4 cup. But don't get me wrong, with one cup this pie is phenomenal. I also tweaked by using 1/4 cup of half & half and 3/4 cup of 2% milk. I used sweetened coconut flakes. The result was a beautiful pale yellow custard. Creamy & smooth. I made an incredible butter pie crust from Allrecipes. The crust put the pie over the top. My sister, who doesn't eat pie crust, made sure she got every crumb. I received numerous compliments on the pie. It is a winner! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I had a craving for a coconut pie and chose this recipe for its simplicity and ingredients I had on hand. As many suggested I decreased the sugar to 1 cup and increased the coconut to 1-1/2 cups. I baked it for the full 50 minutes but probably should've covered the top with foil for part of the baking time as it browned and the filling was just barely set. Great taste. I will try it again and maybe adjust the baking time.

My wife never wanted to try this, now it's one of her favorite deserts! Like others I cut the sugar to 1 cup, and it's still plenty sweet. I also substitute half and half for the milk, and use 3 TBS of flour. Simple to make and delicious.

Really glad I found this recipe. I will definitely make again and again. I read others' reviews and used a few of their pointers. I used 3 eggs instead of 2. I only used 1 cup of sugar (we like desserts that are a little less sweet AND my husband is borderline diabetic. I used coconut milk instead of whole milk - but when I make it again, I probably will use half and half. I also used unsweetened coconut in the filling but sweetened on the top (probably more like 1/4 Cup.

I only used 3/4 cup of sugar. I also used 1/2 cup of whipping cream and 1/2 cup of coconut milk. I added a tsp of nutmeg. I also creamed the butter with the sugar first and separately whipped the cream till it was half way to whip cream and then added the coconut milk. Combined the creamed butted and milk along with the other ingredients.

I wish I had read the reviews prior to making. Despite mixing thoroughly the ingredients separated making the consistency totally wrong. Personally speaking it has too much sugar, too much coconut (and i love cocunut) and not enough flour. I will try again with a few changes based on the other reviews. It also was way too dark, maybe should be cooked on a lower setting as it looked almost burnt once it was set.
We loved this pie! I only used half the sugar as suggested and it was still very sweet. I also made it gluten free by using a GF pie shell and using corn starch instead of flour

I made this pie yesterday & it is delicious. I did cut the suger to a little under 1 cup, the butter to a 1/2 stick based on other reviews . I used evaporated milk , a frozen pie crust , put aluminum foil on the ridge of the crust & baked at 350 for 40 min. & 300 for 10 min. Turned out beautiful. Don't know why some others had problems like runny custard. Pie was perfect & a keeper in my recipes!
Too sweet and didn’t turn out like custard
Just like mama used to make
Tried this three times and twice the custard would not set up. The center of the pie was a liquid mess!
Fist time I made it it was A little too sweet so this time I made it with Spends and it was great! Highly recommend this recipe!
Very good recipe but the other commenters are correct - use half the sugar. this is way too sweet. Otherwise, very easy to make.

The pie was easy, looked good..but way too sweet. I would also increase the amount of custard, and go to 3/4 of a cup of coconut and substitute coconut extract for the vanilla maybe cut the sugar way down and cut in some coco lopez. 😁

The pie was delicious, but after reading other comments I cut back to 1 cup of sugar, it was still rich so next time I'll try 3/4 cup. I'm thinking maybe the poster used unsweetened coconut and made up for it with extra sugar? Either way, I can highly recommend this recipe
